AL.primaryRunoffRule: If no candidate gets a majority, the top two advance to a runoff.

AR.primaryRunoffRule: If no candidate gets a majority, the top two advance to a runoff.

GA.primaryRunoffRule: If no candidate gets a majority, the top two advance to a runoff.
GA.generalRunoffRule: If the threshold is not met, a runoff/second round can occur.
GA.notes: Georgia also uses a general-election runoff if no candidate gets more than 50%.

LA.primaryThresholdLabel: Closed-party-primary offices: >50%; open-primary offices: >50% to win outright
LA.primaryRunoffRule: Closed-party-primary offices: if no one gets a majority, top two in the party advance to a runoff. Open-primary offices: if no one gets a majority in the first round, the top two advance to the second round.
LA.generalThresholdLabel: Open-primary offices: >50% avoids second round; closed-party-primary offices general election is plurality
LA.generalRunoffRule: If the threshold is not met, a runoff/second round can occur.
LA.notes: Beginning in 2026, U.S. Senate, U.S. House, Louisiana Supreme Court, PSC, and BESE use closed party primaries. Most other state, parish, and municipal offices remain in Louisiana's open-primary system.

MS.primaryRunoffRule: If no candidate gets a majority, the top two advance to a runoff.
MS.generalRunoffRule: If the threshold is not met, a runoff/second round can occur.
MS.notes: Mississippi also uses a general-election runoff for statewide offices if no candidate gets more than 50%.

NC.primaryThresholdLabel: >30% in a single-office race (30% + 1 vote); grouped contests use a 30% formula
NC.primaryRunoffRule: A second primary is not automatic. If the first-place candidate falls short of the threshold, the second-place candidate may request a second primary.
NC.notes: North Carolina law defines a 'substantial plurality' at 30% for single-office races. Ballotpedia's summary page appears stale on this point; the statute and NCSL summary reflect the current 30% rule.

OK.primaryRunoffRule: If no candidate gets a majority, the top two advance to a runoff.

SC.primaryRunoffRule: If no candidate gets a majority, the top two advance to a runoff.

SD.primaryThresholdLabel: >35% in gubernatorial/U.S. House/U.S. Senate races with 3+ candidates
SD.primaryRunoffRule: Runoff only for governor, U.S. House, and U.S. Senate primaries with three or more candidates. Otherwise, no separate runoff.
SD.notes: If no candidate in one of those races gets more than 35%, a runoff is held between the top vote-getters.

TX.primaryRunoffRule: If no candidate gets a majority, the top two advance to a runoff.
